title: Ownership + Contracts: The Power Couple
story: A CTO once said: '90% of our production bugs are logic errors, not crashes. Contracts catch the logic errors. The borrow checker catches the crashes. Together, they cover almost everything.' That CTO's team went from 47 incidents/month to 2.
why: Contracts catch LOGIC bugs (division by zero, invalid state). Ownership catches MEMORY bugs (use-after-free, data races). Together they make almost all bugs impossible.
analogy: Ownership is the fence around the factory (keeps intruders out). Contracts are the quality inspectors at each station (catches defects before they ship). Both are needed for safe production.
try_it: List every type of bug you can think of: null pointer, buffer overflow, division by zero, race condition, use-after-free, integer overflow, logic error, infinite loop. For each, mark whether ownership or contracts catch it. What's left? Those are the bugs you must test for.
tips: Ownership catches ~50% of typical C/C++ bugs (memory-related)
The remaining ~10% requires testing and formal verification
Together, ownership + contracts make XIOM one of the safest systems languages
common_mistakes: Thinking contracts replace ownership — they're complementary, not redundant
Writing contracts but ignoring borrow errors — the compiler is trying to help you
Assuming contracts catch ALL bugs — algorithms and business logic still need tests
